svg.title: Dependency updates flow through the framework, not around it — the rendered renovate config centralizes .config updates in the framework
svg.text: Dependency updates flow through the framework, not
Scenario: the rendered renovate config centralizes .config updates in the framework

g.text: Given a generated project carries the framework's centralized renovate
config
.config tooling is owned by THIS framework repo — a generated project must NOT receive
per-tool Renovate MRs, only the framework-evolution MR. The pixel baseline is the actual
rendered config: a re-added rule for one specific tool would show up immediately.
When the config passes the real renovate validator
renovate-config-validator itself checks the rendered config, doing far more than a plain
JSON.parse would.
Then turning automerge off still passes the same validator
The automerge-off branch of the template is real, valid config too.
And a downstream project's renovate ignores stale framework-owned
.config drift
Off-camera: a freshly generated project with every framework-owned .config pin downgraded to
a stale value. Renovate's own extraction summary then lists no .config file — the downstream
project never re-tracks a framework tool.
And a downstream project's renovate tracks its own outdated project
dependency
A separate freshly generated project, this time with an outdated base image added under
project/: its extraction summary picks up the project/ Dockerfile — project/** is exactly
what a generated project is meant to track.
And the framework repo's own renovate detects that same stale .config
drift
The SAME .config downgrade, run in a throwaway framework checkout instead of a generated
project: here renovate MUST detect it — the framework owns .config and tracks its own tool
versions. Downstream ignores, the framework evolves them.
